relocated.semantics: A relocated row adds a second pairing key to its base row: the masked file, form, entry, literal and line span of the row with the record's columns and post-base line SHA-256; a row pairs with one occurrence at most through all its keys; the line number is not part of the key; a change of the post-base line voids the key and the occurrence is reported again. A relocation is not a review: the row keeps its rule, disposition and post-migration obligations, and derive/reviewed.mjs --write never rewrites the records.
rejected: (b) reviewed records: the three tokens are business literals of the navigation family (rows of rules R-144 and R-147), not generic words; a business literal is never reviewed (README design decision 18)

valueChanges.old: Business-policy scan lexicon of the finding #24 occurrence ledger (DESIGN.md:863, 872, 874). No entry writes a scanned literal: every literal is matched through the SHA-256 of its normalised key (matchers regex with hashes, window, brand); a regex matcher without hashes is a structural pattern that names no literal. derive/scan.mjs is the normative implementation. Forms: path (the repository-relative path, line 0), raw (each line), token (JavaScript and JSON constant strings with escapes decoded, adjacent constant fragments joined across + on any number of lines and constant template substitutions folded), decoded (markup character references, CSS escapes and percent escapes, also inside JavaScript constants). Matches of one entry are leftmost-longest and never overlap; every match is one occurrence. reviewed (format /3): occurrences of block B sealed expectation files that were reviewed token by token as generic words, published legacy API values or homographs; in strict mode the scanner does not report an occurrence bound by a reviewed record to its exact file (path SHA-256 and file SHA-256) and span; no entry, matcher or hash is removed.

Forms: path (the repository-relative path, line 0), raw (each line), token (JavaScript and JSON constant strings with escapes decoded, adjacent constant fragments joined across + on any number of lines and constant template substitutions folded), decoded (markup character references, CSS escapes and percent escapes, also inside JavaScript constants). Matches of one entry are leftmost-longest and never overlap; every match is one occurrence. reviewed (format /3): occurrences of block B sealed expectation files that were reviewed token by token as generic words, published legacy API values or homographs; in strict mode the scanner does not report an occurrence bound by a reviewed record to its exact file (path SHA-256 and file SHA-256) and span; no entry, matcher or hash is removed. relocated (format /4): base ledger rows whose source line a block B edit changed after the base without touching their span, each with the post-base columns and line SHA-256 of the same occurrence (README "Reviewed occurrences", "Relocated base rows"); the integration scan and the probe rescan pair an occurrence with its base row through them, the scanner does not read them, and a relocated row keeps its rule and disposition.

new.note: Relocated base rows of the integration zero-literal scan (README "Reviewed occurrences", "Relocated base rows"). A record continues one base ledger row (row) whose source line a block B edit changed after the base without touching the row's span: line, column, endLine and endColumn give the post-base position of the same occurrence and lineSha256 the SHA-256 of the post-base line; file, form, entry, family, literal, key and the span length are the row's, and rule, category, consumer, targetRef and disposition repeat its classification. edit names the block B commit and every base row of the same base line whose span the edit replaced, with the post-base columns and the SHA-256 of the replacement: the post-base line is the base line with those spans substituted, and the row's columns move by the length change of the replacements before it. The integration scan (derive/reviewed.mjs) and the probe rescan (probe-expectations.json#/probe2/trackedRescan) pair an occurrence with the base row through the record's key (masked file, form, entry, literal, column, endColumn, line span and lineSha256) exactly as through the row's base key, and a row pairs with one occurrence at most through all its keys; the line number is not part of the key. A relocation is not a review: the row keeps its rule, disposition and post-migration obligations, a business literal is never reviewed, and any change of the post-base line voids the key. verifiedAt names the tree and the file bytes at which the record was verified; derive/base-check.mjs checks each record against the base line of its row and the seal test against the base row and the current file.
